newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European feeds market on hold ahead of USDA data.
newsitem.headline: European feeds market on hold ahead of USDA data.

text.p: The European cash market for meals and feeds was keenly awaiting the next set of crop figures from the USDA on Monday, with some players predicting bullish stocks data would boost prices.

The higher close on Chicago futures on Friday left physical sellers in Europe this morning offering South American soymeal pellets up to five dollars above previous levels but activity was hampered by the impending U.S. data, traders said.
"Everybody is waiting for the USDA figures," said Arie van Dijk of market statisticians Stigevo. "It's very quiet."
Traders said they expected U.S. ending stocks for soybeans to drop between five and ten million bushels from an already tight projection of 125 million bushels.

Van Dijk favoured the more bullish scenario, with the figure dropping some 10 million bushels but added that the first projection was also expected for next season, which could offset any market impact.
"The interesting point will be the first sign of ending stocks for next season. It is possible that a bullish figure for the old crop will be compensated by a bearish one for the new crop," he said.
Traders also noted that the last time that the figures were downwardly revised, the market in Chicago dropped and this has increased the willingness to stay sidelined this time around.

Looking at the vessel arrival lists for north-west Europe, traders noted that there were few arrivals for products such as corngluten and citruspulp pellets, which could cause some tightness in those markets.
However, others said consumers were pretty well covered and demand for cattle feed was slack in any case as cows were now being put out to pasture.
"There are not many arrivals but there are stocks in the domestic market. Some compounders bought citrus and corngluten a few months ago at much cheaper prices," Van Dijk said.
Elsewhere, the improving situation for the European grain crop was a market talking point, with the belief growing that the crop will be a good one.
In France, the recent rainfall has given rise to the hope that the crop could even approach the 1996 record harvest.
The dollar moved up in the afternoon as well, which was also cited as a reason keeping a lid on activity this afternoon.

May Argentine sunmeal pellets traded at $146 a tonne cif Rotterdam. Afloat Malaysian palmkernel expellers changed hands at $102 a tonne cif Rotterdam and EU high protein soymeal at $345 a tonne fob Hamburg.
No trades were reported in other products.--KAREL LUIMES +31 20 504 5832
